Not re-emitting; adding violations.rs to that finding's blast radius via review-note instead.

NEW FINDING 1 (assign_violation missing membership check): backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/violations.rs:313-331 assign_violation accepts req.assigned_to: Uuid and passes it straight to backend/crates/db/src/repositories/violations.rs:383 assign_violation(violation_id, org_id, assigned_to). The SQL UPDATE scopes by (id, organization_id) but has NO guard that assigned_to belongs to organization_id - FK is to users(id) global. A Manager in org A can assign a violation to a user in org B (or any user id they guess). Not catastrophic (write is confined to org A's own violation row) but it (a) lets a Manager plant an inconsistent `assigned_to` that other handlers will later surface, (b) can leak existence of arbitrary user ids via downstream rendering, and (c) matches the exact IDOR-adjacent class the recent community/violations hardening work has been eliminating.

NEW FINDING 2 (test-gap: no cross-tenant IDOR suite for violations.rs): the recent churn landed violations_role_authz_tests.rs (role-based 403 coverage) and community_cross_tenant_idor_tests.rs (cross-tenant 404 coverage for community.rs). There is no symmetric cross-tenant IDOR suite for violations.rs, even though 10+ privileged mutations take resource ids straight from the URL path (violation_id, action_id, evidence_id, appeal_id). The role-gate alone does not prove tenant isolation - a Manager in org A guessing an action_id from org B must still get 404 and perform no write. The repo scoping (via _for_org helpers / `AND organization_id = $2` WHERE clauses) looks correct on inspection, but there is no IG3 regression test guarding it; a future repo refactor could regress silently.

FINDINGS NOT EMITTED (would duplicate yesterday or are intentional-design): (a) raw sqlx::Error leak via internal_error(&format!(...)) on violations.rs - same class as code-review-api-handlers-db-error-leak 2026-10-25; (b) create_appeal / add_comment are ungated by role - intentional per the module docstring at violations.rs:50.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/violations.rs:313-331 assign_violation(Path(violation_id), Json(AssignRequest{assigned_to})) calls repo with (violation_id, org_id, req.assigned_to) with NO check that assigned_to is a member of org_id.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/violations.rs:383-405 UPDATE scopes by (id=$1, organization_id=$2) but binds $3 assigned_to with no FK/scoping to org - users(id) is global, so a Manager in org A can set assigned_to to a user in org B or any guessed uuid; FK will accept it.

Fix: add a `is_user_member_of_org(assigned_to, org_id)` guard in the handler (or inside repo) returning 400/404 on cross-org assignee - mirror the pattern used in the recently-landed community cross-tenant IDOR fixes.
backend/servers/api-server/tests/suites/violations_role_authz_tests.rs (242 LOC, this run's top churn file) covers role-authz 403s but NOT cross-tenant 404 on resource-id paths.

backend/servers/api-server/tests/suites/community_cross_tenant_idor_tests.rs (130 LOC, same run's #3 churn file) establishes the IG3 pattern for sibling router community.rs - no analogous suite exists for violations.rs.

Uncovered mutation surface in backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/violations.rs taking path ids: assign_violation (313), add_evidence (337), delete_evidence (375), create_action (403), update_action (460), mark_action_sent (485), record_payment (505), update_appeal (599), decide_appeal (626). Each should assert cross-tenant 404 + no write and same-tenant 2xx + write happens.
